Subject: Arroyo Precision Works — fast, careful, and they actually read the drawing

I’m a postdoc in the Ostrowski group, and we ordered an adapter plate and a light baffle tube from Arroyo for our near-IR camera. The camera is going to the Palomar 200-inch run on Nov. 18, so this was one of those jobs where a late part would have cost us the whole trip. Arroyo quoted 21 days and we had the parts in 9 days from PO to delivery. The big vendor we use for simpler work quoted six weeks. That difference was not a small thing for us.

The quality was right on the first try. At our fit test on Nov. 9, the plate went onto the dewar with all eight screws in and no forcing. Flatness across the face was under 0.01 mm on the dial indicator. The baffle threads were smooth, the anodize was even with no bare spots, and a 300 s dark test with the lab lights on showed no light leak, same as a closed dewar. For a near-IR camera, fit and stray light are not cosmetic details, and all of it checked out.

The part that really sold me is that they caught a mistake in my drawing before they cut metal. The bolt circle on sheet 2 was marked 4.125 while every other dimension was in mm. Ruben and Tiff noticed that 4.125 mm would have put the screws inside the bore and asked me to confirm before they started. That was my error — I copied it from an old drawing of the previous camera — and I want to be clear about that. A shop that reads the drawing carefully and asks before cutting is worth a lot. If they had just machined what was on the page, we would have had scrap and probably lost the run.

Ruben also drove the finished parts to Robinson Lab himself on his way to a supplier in Glendale, at no charge, so we had them in hand before the weekend. I almost hugged him at the loading dock. Communication was quick and clear the whole way through, and the inspection sheet came with the parts.

I’d happily use Arroyo again for instrument work, and I’d like purchasing to add them to the preferred vendor list. Five stars.

— Lin Wei
